tb21_profile.skill: Parse the SQLite on-disk format by hand - file header, page headers, leaf table B-tree cells, record varints and serial types - and salvage every complete row from a file that sqlite3 itself refuses to open because the tail is missing
tb21_profile.domain: SQLite internals and binary file-format forensics; Python byte-level parsing
tb21_profile.task_form: recover/repair-corrupted-data: maximise recovered rows from a damaged binary and emit them as structured JSON

notes: CalibForge wins this one outright and takes 7 of the final 10: it has three tasks that parse the raw SQLite file format directly (damaged header in a sector dump, deleted-record recovery from pages, freeblock forensics on leaf B-tree pages) plus a whole family of binary-layout salvage tasks, most graded strong. Nothing comparable exists in the v1 pool - TMax's best is repairing the 16-byte magic header and fixing a WAL recovery tool in C (both real transfer, both kept), and its other entries are generic binary-format parsing. Terminal-Lego is thin here: mostly sqlite3-API usage tasks, with only the Vim swap-file recovery and struct framing tasks carrying any of the skill; I could not find 10 strongly defensible Lego candidates and the tail is scored 2. Recursive-Task-Synthesis and TerminalWorld likewise have no on-disk-format recovery task and their lists are padded with database-creation chores. SWE-Rebench's pfp family (a binary-template interpreter doing LEB128 reads until EOF) is a better fit than anything in SWE-Smith except pyasn1's TLV decoder and gunicorn's length-vs-EOF readers.
